items.followUp: What does the law of conservation of momentum state for an isolated system?

rubric.why: An isolated system has no external force acting on it, or equivalently has zero net external force.
rubric.description: Defines an isolated system by the absence of external force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent condition.

rubric.why: The total momentum of an isolated system is conserved.
rubric.description: States that the system’s total momentum remains constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct statement of momentum conservation.

modelAnswer: An isolated system is one on which no external force acts; equivalently, the net external force on it is zero.
The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.

items.followUp: State two applications of solar panels.

rubric.why: A solar panel is made by electrically connecting several solar cells.
rubric.description: Explains how a solar panel is formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a panel consists of connected solar cells.

rubric.why: Solar panels convert sunlight into electrical energy, which can power devices and equipment.
rubric.description: States the energy conversion or gives a suitable use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that panels generate electrical energy from sunlight or giving a valid application.

modelAnswer: A solar panel is formed by connecting many solar cells together, in series and/or parallel.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electrical energy and are used, for example, in satellites and calculators.

items.followUp: A force has perpendicular components of 6 N and 8 N. Find its magnitude and direction relative to the 6 N component.

rubric.why: The force is resolved into two mutually perpendicular components.
rubric.description: Identifies the two perpendicular components using suitable symbols.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying perpendicular components such as Fx and Fy.

rubric.why: The components and resultant form a right-angled triangle, so the Pythagorean theorem applies.
rubric.description: Writes the Pythagorean relation for the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation between the resultant and its perpendicular components.

rubric.why: The positive square root gives the magnitude of the resultant force.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for the resultant magnitude and its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the magnitude formula, with the result expressed in newtons when components are in newtons.

rubric.why: The component ratio determines the direction of the resultant relative to Fx.
rubric.description: Gives the correct relation for the direction of the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction relation.

modelAnswer: Let Fx and Fy be the two perpendicular components of the force, measured in newtons.
By Pythagoras’ theorem, R² = Fx² + Fy².
Therefore, the magnitude of the resultant force is R = √(Fx² + Fy²) N.
Its direction relative to Fx is θ = tan⁻¹(Fy/Fx).
